cards.info: What algebraic condition must be met for a function to be even?
cards.backInfo: The function must satisfy $f(-x) = f(x)$ for all $x$ in the domain.

cards.info: Across which axis is the graph of an even function symmetric?
cards.backInfo: The graph of an even function is symmetric across the y-axis.

cards.info: What algebraic condition defines an odd function?
cards.backInfo: An odd function satisfies the condition $f(-x) = -f(x)$.

cards.info: What type of symmetry does the graph of an odd function have?
cards.backInfo: It has rotational symmetry about the origin $(0,0)$.

cards.info: How do you find the vertical asymptotes of a rational function?
cards.backInfo: Solve for the values of $x$ that make the denominator equal to zero.

cards.info: What must be true for a denominator zero to be a vertical asymptote?
cards.backInfo: The value must make the denominator zero but NOT make the numerator zero.

cards.info: What is the horizontal asymptote if the numerator degree is less than the denominator?
cards.backInfo: The horizontal asymptote is the x-axis, which is the line $y = 0$.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing how to determine horizontal vs oblique asymptotes based on polynomial degrees.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/0a9b3399-9f32-4c20-b226-e6b50824ac9a-1786505882627-634.webp)

cards.info: How is the horizontal asymptote found when the numerator and denominator degrees are equal?
cards.backInfo: The horizontal asymptote is $y = \text{(leading coefficient of numerator)} / \text{(leading coefficient of denominator)}$.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing how to determine horizontal vs oblique asymptotes based on polynomial degrees.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/0a9b3399-9f32-4c20-b226-e6b50824ac9a-1786505882627-634.webp)

cards.info: When does a rational function have an oblique (slant) asymptote?
cards.backInfo: When the degree of the numerator is exactly one greater than the degree of the denominator.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing how to determine horizontal vs oblique asymptotes based on polynomial degrees.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/0a9b3399-9f32-4c20-b226-e6b50824ac9a-1786505882627-634.webp)

cards.info: Is a horizontal asymptote guaranteed if the numerator degree is higher than the denominator?
cards.backInfo: No; if the numerator degree is higher, there is no horizontal asymptote.

cards.info: If $f(x) = x^4 + x^2 + 5$, what is $f(-x)$?
A graph is symmetric across the y-axis. What is its parity?
cards.backInfo: The function is an even function.

cards.info: If $f(x) = x^3$, what is the relationship between $f(-x)$ and $f(x)$?
cards.backInfo: $f(-x) = (-x)^3 = -x^3$, so $f(-x) = -f(x)$, making it an odd function.

cards.info: What graphical symmetry is shown by the function $y = x^3$?
cards.backInfo: It shows rotational symmetry about the origin $(0,0)$.

cards.info: Find the vertical asymptotes for $f(x) = \frac{1}{x^2 - 9}$.
cards.backInfo: Setting $x^2 - 9 = 0$ gives vertical asymptotes at $x = 3$ and $x = -3$.

cards.info: What occurs at $x=2$ for $f(x) = \frac{x-2}{x^2-4}$?
cards.backInfo: A hole (removable discontinuity) occurs because $x=2$ makes both the numerator and denominator zero.

cards.info: Determine the horizontal asymptote of $f(x) = \frac{5x + 2}{x^2 - 1}$.
cards.backInfo: Since the numerator degree (1) is less than the denominator degree (2), $y = 0$.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing how to determine horizontal vs oblique asymptotes based on polynomial degrees.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/0a9b3399-9f32-4c20-b226-e6b50824ac9a-1786505882627-634.webp)

cards.info: Find the horizontal asymptote of $f(x) = \frac{6x^2 + 1}{2x^2 - 5}$.
cards.backInfo: The degrees are equal, so $y = 6/2$, which simplifies to $y = 3$.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing how to determine horizontal vs oblique asymptotes based on polynomial degrees.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/0a9b3399-9f32-4c20-b226-e6b50824ac9a-1786505882627-634.webp)

cards.info: Does $f(x) = \frac{x^2 + 1}{x - 1}$ have a horizontal or oblique asymptote?
cards.backInfo: It has an oblique asymptote because the numerator degree (2) is exactly one greater than the denominator degree (1).
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing how to determine horizontal vs oblique asymptotes based on polynomial degrees.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/0a9b3399-9f32-4c20-b226-e6b50824ac9a-1786505882627-634.webp)

cards.info: What is the end behavior of $f(x) = \frac{x^3}{x+1}$?
cards.backInfo: The function grows toward infinity without a linear asymptote because the numerator degree is more than one greater than the denominator.
